text:
maeve: heads up — after the midnight merge I'm seeing a sharp p95 decode latency jump on canary (service:x-runner). started ~00:06 UTC, coincides with deploy 9f3c2a7.

arjun: ugh. saw the alert too. p95 from ~120ms -> 420ms for short-seq traffic. p50 fine. looks like tail-only.

lina: any kernel fallback in traces? could be attention kernel selector flip.

maeve: profile attached (quick flame snippet):
```
flamegraph: decode -> attn_kernel_slow -> memcpy_kv -> matmul_small
hotspot: memcpy_kv 38%
```

jules: ci-bot reported a perf-test failure on the nightly suite: `decode_p95_shortseq > threshold`. link: https://ci/redwood/9876

ci-bot: [perf-suite] test decode_p95_shortseq FAILED (baseline 150ms -> 410ms). commit 9f3c2a7 triggered.

arjun: looks like the fused-op reorder in PR #4823 (author: pat) changed kernel scheduling heuristics; scheduler now prefers fused-attn path but falls back for certain shapes and does expensive memcopy during fallback.

pat: I added that reorder to reduce kernel launches for long sequences; didn't expect short-seq decode to regress. My local perf didn't catch it.

maeve: repro command I ran: `RUNTIME_PROF=1 ./bin/serve --model gpt-small --seq 32 --batching fast` then `perf record -g -p $(pgrep serve)` and `perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl`.

lina: can you dump KV cache eviction stats? if fallback copies KV out it could thrash and rebuild prefix causing tail blowup.

maeve: KV evictions spike in the same window. sample: `kv.evictions=421 -> 4600` after 9f3c2a7. prefix-recompute time increased ~3x.

jules: suggestion: hold the rollout and revert 9f3c2a7 on canary while we bisect. ops-bot, can you stop further canaries?

ops-bot: Rolling canary hold: targeting service:x-runner. New deploys blocked. :white_check_mark:

arjun: bisect plan: revert the fused-op reorder locally then run the short-seq perf harness across the commit range (9f3c2a7 -> parent). If revert fixes, we craft a narrow patch to avoid fallback memcopy.

pat: I'll push a quick revert candidate: `git revert -m 1 9f3c2a7 --no-edit` on branch `hotfix/revert-fuse-reorder`.

maeve: can we also add an integration perf guard that runs short-seq decode at premerge? CI flaky but better than nothing. ci-bot can gate perf threshold for this path.

ci-bot: Proposed: add `decode_p95_shortseq` to the critical perf gates. Will run nightly and post diffs.

lina: also want to add a microbenchmark that exercises the fallback path with KV cache stress — reproduce locally with `--kv-heavy` flag. saves time vs full e2e.

arjun: agreed. after revert we'll run `./bench/decode_shortseq --kv-heavy --iters 5000` and compare flamegraphs.

pat: reverted on canary and pushed hotfix candidate. request review from arjun and maeve. PR: https://phab/revision/D3457

maeve: after revert canary p95 dropped back to ~140ms. KV evictions normalized. :relieved:

jules: nice. keep the hold until we ship a proper fix + smaller change to kernel selector.

arjun: next steps: 1) bisect to find minimal diff that triggers memcpy fallback, 2) add a selector guard for small seqs to prefer the stable kernel, 3) add perf gate + microbench. I'll own 1+2.

pat: I'll help with 3 and write the `--kv-heavy` bench.

maeve: thanks all. filing a short incident note and linking the revert PR + flamegraphs.

jules: incident note: https://wiki/redwood/incidents/2026-03-18-decode-tail-spike (draft).

ops-bot: Canary hold remains active until `hotfix/revert-fuse-reorder` is promoted to stable or superset fix is merged.

maeve: will follow up in morning with bisect findings. good night everyone. :sleeping:
